topic: Unconscious task-switching as a symptom of raised dopamine threshold
body:
**You sit down to work. Within 90 seconds, you're on a different tab. You didn't decide to go there.**

That's not distraction. That's threshold behaviour. Your brain has been trained to expect a certain level of stimulation — and a blank document or a hard problem doesn't meet it. So the system routes around the discomfort automatically, before you've consciously chosen anything.

This is why willpower-based solutions fail. You're not fighting a habit. You're fighting a calibration. Your brain isn't broken — it's doing exactly what it was trained to do in every other context of your life. It's seeking higher input.

The fix isn't more focus. It's a lower baseline.

When you reduce the stimulus frequency across your whole environment — not just during work sessions — the threshold drops. Ordinary hard tasks start to meet it again. That's the reset.

One thing you can do today: before any work session, sit with nothing for two minutes. No music, no podcast, no phone. You're not meditating. You're lowering the floor before you start.

Full protocol is linked in bio.
